The *Kañjikadāyikāvimānavatthu* (Vv 43), translated as *Rice-Gruel-Giver’s Mansion*, is a canonical verse text in the *Vimānavatthu* section of the Pali canon. In this discourse, a deva describes the celestial happiness and reward gained as a result of having offered medicine to the Buddha.

 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse within the collection and its commentary [DharmaNexus]. The commentary, *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, shares substantial portions of the text (§0.4–9.4), while verse formulas are shared closely with other *Vimānavatthu* texts, most notably *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33, §0.4–3.3), *Ācāmadāyikāvimānavatthu* (Vv 20, §6.1–10.1), *Caturitthivimānavatthu* (Vv 45), and *Alomavimānavatthu* (Vv 42) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns verse segments (such as §6.2–6.3) with Tibetan passages found in the *Caityapradakṣiṇagāthā* (D0321) [DharmaNexus].
